title: Kenyan Coconut Cassava Bites
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Coconut Cassava Bites — cubes of boiled cassava coated in a sweet, fragrant coconut and sugar mixture with cardamom. A simple coastal Swahili treat that transforms humble cassava into something indulgent and aromatic.
longDesc: Coconut cassava bites are a coastal Kenyan treat that perfectly illustrates the Swahili instinct to improve anything with coconut. Boiled cassava cubes are rolled in a mixture of grated coconut, sugar, and cardamom while still warm — the coconut adheres and the whole thing becomes fragrant, slightly chewy, and deeply satisfying.
ingredients: 600g cassava — peeled, boiled until tender, and cut into bite-sized cubes
1 cup desiccated or freshly grated coconut
steps: Peel and boil cassava as per KEN035. Cut into bite-sized cubes while warm.
Mix coconut, sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl.
While the cassava is still warm, roll each piece in the coconut mixture.
Press the coating gently to adhere.
Arrange on a plate. Serve warm or at room temperature.
chefTips: Coat the cassava while it is still warm — the warmth helps the coconut mixture adhere.
Freshly grated coconut gives a more moist, fragrant result than desiccated.
A tiny drizzle of condensed milk over the coated pieces adds extra sweetness and helps the coating stick.
commonMistakes: Coating cold cassava — the mixture does not adhere well.
Overcooking cassava — it falls apart when coated.
cookingScience: Warm cassava releases surface starch that acts as a natural adhesive for the coconut coating. The warmth also slightly softens the coconut, creating a better texture integration than coating cold cassava.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is one of the most sustainable crops in East Africa.
storage: Consume within 4 hours — the coating softens over time.
culturalNote: Coconut cassava bites are a coastal Swahili treat that showcases the coast's genius for combining two abundant local ingredients into something more than the sum of their parts.
